paper_title: MathOdyssey Benchmarking Mathematical Problem-Solving Skills in Large   Language Models Using Odyssey Math Data
caption: Mathematical problems across educational levels. We curate and categorize problems by difficulty and subject area.
model_annotation: The pie chart represents the distribution of mathematical problems across various subjects and educational levels. The chart is divided into 11 slices, each representing a different category. The slices are labeled with their corresponding subject and educational level, and are colored differently for distinction. The categories and their approximate proportions are: Algebra - Olympiad-level (dark blue, 21%), Algebra - High School (light green, 18%), Combinatorics - Olympiad-level (pink, 10%), Geometry - Olympiad-level (purple, 6%), Number Theory - Olympiad-level (orange, 1%), Geometry - High School (brown, 4%), Pre-Calculus - High School (light brown, 14%), Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra - University-level (pink, 6%), Calculus and Analysis - University-level (gray, 6%), Differential Equations - University-level (yellow, 4%), Probability - University-level (light blue, 5%), and Statistics - University-level (teal, 4%). The chart does not include a legend, but the labels are connected to their corresponding slices with lines. The slices are not ordered in any particular way, and no slice is visually emphasized. The proportions are also numerically labeled outside the chart, making it easy to determine the exact percentage of each category.
